newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crude business gauges arb economics.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crude business gauges arb economics.

text.p: U.S. foreign crude business was subdued Monday, continuing to assess the economics in bringing over transatlantic barrels to the U.S.
January Brent against the December West Texas Intermediate was around the 90-95 cents level, while the corresponding February was slightly wider at 95 cts-$1.00.
Wet Brent was sold Monday at Jan Brent plus 15 cts for Dec 10-12 dates, improving some 10 cts on Friday business.
Demand was seen improving for North Sea barrels, but traders said there needed to be further movement in the arbitrage before domestic U.S. grades lost their favor.
Latin American business was called quiet Monday, with talk that Tripetrol was offering Oriente for Jan 20-30 at Jan WTI minus $2.60 the featured topic.
Paper Brent trades in the U.S. aftermarket window saw two deals for the same full boat of January Brent sell at a one cent difference.
Traders said a Wall Street trader bought a Jan Brent at $22.76 a barrel, then turned around and sold it to the same party for $22.75. The prices compared to an IPE Jan Brent settlement at $22.61.
Other deals saw 100 lots of Jan Brent trade at $22.60, and a further partial parcel sell at $22.62. A pair of paper spreads were done: a Dec/Jan at plus 58 cts and a Jan/Feb at plus 54 cts.
